svg.title: A day of scheduled turns over one memory
svg.desc: Five cron jobs and the heartbeat each start one agent turn in their own session. The turn reads the behavior files, reads and writes canonical memory through the memory tools, and hands web lookups to the search agent. Jobs set to delivery: announce reach web clients and DM sessions; git sync commits the workspace on its own schedule.

g.text: Hover a box for what it does; its connections light up. Click it to open the recipe section.
Inside a rendered document this image is static. Click it to open the interactive SVG.

svg.text: SCHEDULE · A DAY OF THE PERSONAL ASSISTANT
A day of scheduled turns over one memory
Every job fire gets its own session and one agent turn. Only delivery: announce reaches your phone. Cron times are server-local.

g.class: e join f-nightly f-briefing f-weekly f-inbox f-journal t-turn
e main f-nightly f-briefing f-weekly f-inbox f-journal t-turn

g.text: nightly-reflection · reads errors.md and the canonical learnings, checks earlier reflections, saves 3-5 insights with memory_apply
Skips when errors.md is empty and nothing relevant turns up. A per-job model: or effort: override is available.
morning-briefing · reads USER.md and SOUL.md, searches memory for reminders, searches the web, and announces a mobile-sized briefing
The announce goes to your phone through an active DM session, and to the web UI.
weekly-review · optional entry in the config: summarizes the week from canonical observations and reflections under topic weekly-review
Comment it out if you do not want it; each pillar is independent.
knowledge-inbox · searches the web for each Topics to Track entry, checks memory for duplicates, saves new findings with memory_observe
Large pages come back content-guarded, so the job should note when a source was truncated.
daily-journal · records notable observations with memory_observe; it cannot read your main chat session
It works from the behavior files and memory. Curation is opt-in: only the memory-curation job revises or removes entries.
one turn per job fire, own session
model: agent.model, or the job's own
guards stay on: command, file, network
agent turn · one agent turn per job fire, in an isolated session; guards check its tool calls as in any turn
Jobs share no session state: what a job wants to keep it saves to memory, and the next job finds it with memory_search.
behavior files · SOUL.md holds identity and Topics to Track, USER.md your timezone and goals, AGENTS.md safety and retrieval rules
AGENTS.md makes the agent search memory before the web. HEARTBEAT.md is the heartbeat job's checklist.
canonical memory · MEMORY.md index, memory/topics, daily observation files, learnings.md and errors.md in the workspace
Search uses the PostgreSQL lexical index by default; hybrid search is opt-in. The agent cannot write errors.md.
search agent · the agents.search entry in the config: a cheap model with only WebSearch and WebFetch
Its result passes content-guard before it returns to the turn, so large pages may arrive truncated.
the open web · everything the search agent fetches
AGENTS.md tells it to prefer authoritative sources and not follow file downloads or executables.
heartbeat · built-in job: reads the HEARTBEAT.md checklist and runs it as one turn; a missing or empty file skips the fire
Results are logged, not saved to a chat session. It does not run git sync.
announce targets · delivery: announce goes to connected web clients and to the active DM sessions of registered channels
It does not reach contacts with no active session, and group sessions are skipped. Use delivery: webhook to push to an endpoint.
git-sync · built-in job: commits workspace changes on workspace.git_sync.interval_minutes, default 30
It runs whether or not the heartbeat is on, and pushes when push_enabled is set and an origin exists.
git remote origin · the remote you add with git remote add origin; optional
Without it the workspace stays a local repository and git sync only commits.
